subject: math

objective.text: Estimate differences by rounding. Pick a way to round that gives a close estimate, then check your exact answer.

explanations.title: Round both numbers
explanations.text: 362 minus 189: round to hundreds, 400 minus 200 is 200. Round to tens, 360 minus 190 is 170.

explanations.title: Round only the part
explanations.text: 189 is close to 200. Keep 362 and subtract 200: 162. The real answer is 173.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 1 (S: Let's just round the part.)

explanations.title: Round the same way for subtraction
explanations.text: When both numbers round the same way, the distance between them stays about the same. That gives a close estimate.

explanations.title: Add the same to both
explanations.text: For 532 minus 198, add 2 to both: 534 minus 200 is 334. The difference does not change.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 2 (S: ... add 2 to both numbers so I have 534 – 200)

examples.title: 362 minus 189
examples.text: Hundreds estimate 200, tens estimate 170, round-the-part estimate 162. Actual 173. Tens was closest.

examples.title: 349 minus 149
examples.text: Both round down: 300 minus 100 is 200. The actual answer is also 200.

questions.text: 450 liters minus 228 liters equals what number?

hints.text: Round each number first. Then subtract the rounded numbers.
Is the part close to a hundred? Round just the part.
Do both numbers round the same way? Then the estimate stays close.
Find the exact difference with the algorithm. Compare it with your estimate.
Look at the tens digit. 5 tens or more rounds up.
